basis.governing_question: Which ERP should replace Farmácias Lusas's finance, purchasing and inventory systems, and how is it migrated and rolled out to 40 pharmacies and 2 warehouses?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Map requirements and process fit for finance, purchasing and inventory across the pharmacies and warehouses.

gate.label: Requirements sign-off
gate.decision: Approve the requirements and go to vendor selection?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Score ERP vendors against the requirements and build the business case for the vendor that fits best.

gate.label: Vendor selection
gate.decision: Which ERP vendor goes forward into implementation?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Configure the ERP, migrate data, and take it live from a pilot pharmacy and warehouse to all sites.

gate.label: Final acceptance
gate.decision: Approve the ERP as running in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?

workstreams.name: Finance and purchasing needs
workstreams.answers: What must the ERP do for finance and purchasing at the pharmacies and warehouses?
activities: Interview the staff who run finance and purchasing
Map finance and purchasing processes as they run today
List requirements from operational data and documents

workstreams.name: Inventory needs
workstreams.answers: What must the ERP do for inventory in the pharmacies and warehouses?
activities: Interview pharmacy and warehouse staff who manage stock
Map inventory handling in warehouses and pharmacies
List requirements from stock data and documents

workstreams.name: Fit-gap of current systems
workstreams.answers: Where do today's finance, purchasing and inventory systems fall short of the requirements?
activities: Compare today's systems with the requirements
Test gaps with the people who use the systems
Consolidate the requirements for sign-off

workstreams.name: ERP vendor selection
workstreams.answers: Which ERP vendors meet the approved requirements for finance, purchasing and inventory?
activities: Shortlist ERP vendors against the approved requirements
Run demonstrations with pharmacy and warehouse users
Score vendors against each requirement

workstreams.name: ERP business case
workstreams.answers: Does the business case support selecting the leading ERP vendor for Farmácias Lusas?
activities: Gather cost data from today's systems and records
Build the cost and benefit view for shortlisted vendors
Test the case with the CFO and Operations Director

workstreams.name: ERP build and testing
workstreams.answers: Can the ERP be configured and tested for finance, purchasing and inventory?
activities: Configure finance and purchasing, then inventory
Test each area with the people who will use it
Record test results for the readiness review

workstreams.name: Data migration rehearsal
workstreams.answers: Can data from today's systems be migrated and loaded into the configured ERP?
activities: Map and clean data from today's systems
Rehearse the data load and reconcile the results
Agree reconciliation checks with the CFO and IT Manager

workstreams.name: Pilot pharmacy and warehouse
workstreams.answers: Does the ERP run live and stable at the pilot pharmacy and warehouse?
activities: Confirm readiness of the pilot sites before go-live
Load live data and cut over at each pilot site
Track stability and issues with the staff using the ERP

workstreams.name: Rollout waves and run-in
workstreams.answers: Does the ERP run for finance, purchasing and inventory in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?
activities: Load live data and cut over each wave of sites
Roll out wave by wave and track issues with site staff
Run a month-end close with all sites live and review it

deliverables.name: Finance and purchasing requirements and process maps
Consolidated requirements and fit-gap for sign-off
ERP vendor shortlist and demonstration findings
Vendor scoring against the approved requirements
ERP business case with vendor scoring
Finance and purchasing configuration and test record
Inventory configuration and ERP readiness test results
Data migration rehearsal and reconciliation results
Go-live record for the pilot pharmacy and warehouse
Pilot close-out record with open-issue log
Go-live records for the first rollout waves
Rollout status report with open-issue log
Final acceptance pack: all sites and month-end close

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Start the diagnostic and secure access
events.decision: Can the team access finance, purchasing and inventory data and staff from week 1?
agenda: Present the problem statement and the three phases
Review the data and people the diagnostic needs in weeks 1 to 3
Decide how the team gets access to data and staff

events.label: Check-in: process maps
events.purpose: Review process maps and gaps to close
events.decision: Which process areas need more detail before the requirements sign-off?
agenda: Present finance, purchasing and inventory process maps
Review requirements captured and the gaps still open
Decide which process areas need more detail before sign-off

events.label: Requirements sign-off
events.decision: Approve the requirements and go to vendor selection?
agenda: Present the consolidated requirements and fit-gap
Review how the requirements cover finance, purchasing and inventory
Decide whether to approve the requirements and start vendor selection

events.label: Check-in: vendor scoring
events.decision: Which vendors from the scoring go into the business case?
agenda: Present the vendor shortlist and demonstration findings
Review vendor scoring against the approved requirements
Decide which vendors the business case covers

events.label: Vendor selection
events.decision: Which ERP vendor goes forward into implementation?
agenda: Present the business case with vendor scoring
Review vendor scores and demonstration findings
Decide which ERP vendor goes forward into implementation

events.label: Check-in: build progress
events.purpose: Review finance and purchasing build results
events.decision: Which open test findings must close before ERP readiness testing begins?
agenda: Present the finance and purchasing configuration and test record
Review test results and open findings
Decide which findings close before readiness testing

events.label: Workshop 1: pilot readiness
events.purpose: Check readiness before the pilot goes live
events.decision: Go or no-go on the pilot go-live at the pilot pharmacy and warehouse?
agenda: Present inventory configuration and readiness test results
Review data migration rehearsal and reconciliation results
Decide whether the pilot pharmacy and warehouse go live

events.label: Check-in: pilot results
events.purpose: Review pilot results before the first wave
events.decision: Does the pilot stability report support starting the first rollout wave?
agenda: Present the pilot go-live record and stability report
Review pilot stability and issues raised since go-live
Decide whether the first rollout wave starts

events.label: Check-in: pilot close-out
events.purpose: Review pilot close-out and open issues
events.decision: Which open pilot issues must close before the next rollout wave goes live?
agenda: Present the pilot close-out record and open-issue log
Review which pilot issues remain open
Decide which open issues close before the next wave

events.label: Workshop 2: remaining waves
events.purpose: Review first waves and remaining waves
events.decision: Go or no-go on the remaining rollout waves after the first waves' results?
agenda: Present go-live records for the first rollout waves
Review the pilot reports and open-issue log
Decide whether the remaining rollout waves go ahead

events.label: Check-in: rollout status
events.purpose: Review rollout status ahead of acceptance
events.decision: Which open rollout issues must close before final acceptance?
agenda: Present the rollout status report and open-issue log
Review progress toward all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses live
Decide which open issues close before final acceptance

events.label: Final acceptance
events.purpose: Accept the ERP across all sites
events.decision: Approve the ERP as running in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?
agenda: Present the final acceptance pack for all sites and month-end close
Review the rollout status report and remaining open issues
Decide whether to approve the ERP as running across all sites

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given, so every duration is an estimate to confirm before quoting.
Implementation uses the middle of a 33 to 47 week estimate; the top needs areas, pilots, waves and run-in at their longest.
Implementation ends with a 3 to 4 week run-in after the last wave, covering a month-end close; confirm acceptance is judged on all sites live.
Length assumes one migration rehearsal plus live load and cutover at each pilot site and wave; a second rehearsal adds 2 to 3 weeks.
Implementation is added to the technology selection archetype's Diagnostic and Design because the brief includes data migration and rollout to 40 pharmacies and 2 warehouses.
Design assumes shortlist and demonstrations without a formal tender; a tender would add 4 to 6 weeks and should be confirmed.

sub_questions.question: What must the ERP do for finance, purchasing and inventory, and where do today's systems fall short?
Which ERP fits the requirements, and does its business case support selecting it?
Can the ERP be configured, tested and loaded with migrated data for finance, purchasing and inventory?
Can the ERP run live and stable at pilot sites, then in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?

drivers.evidence: roll it out to its 40 pharmacies and 2 warehouses

phases.name: Diagnostic

work.unit: Process area mapped with its requirements

phases.why: Three process areas mapped two at a time, plus start-up and synthesis weeks; inside the archetype's typical 3 to 6 weeks.

phases.name: Design
phases.why: One shortlist, demonstration and scoring round, then a synthesis week; no formal tender assumed. Inside the archetype's typical 4 to 8 weeks.

phases.name: Implementation

work.unit: System configured and tested for one process area
Live data load and cutover at the pilot pharmacy and warehouse
Live data load and cutover per wave; second warehouse in wave 1
Rollout wave of up to 10 sites
Run-in with all pharmacies and warehouses live, including a month-end close

phases.why: Areas configured two at a time, one rehearsal, a pilot at one pharmacy and one warehouse, four waves with cutover each, then a run-in.

sizing.levers: Rollout waves two at a time would save 6 to 8 weeks; configuring all three process areas together would save 4 to 6 more.
